findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate()` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only such method defined in the class hierarchy is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` which requires a `UserModel` parameter. No no-arg overload exists in `UsernameForm`, `UsernamePasswordForm`, `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, or their parents. This will cause a compilation error. The call should likely be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: Passkeys conditional UI no longer set up during initial login (user == null)
findings.body: In `authenticate()`, the webauthn setup condition was changed from being inside the `else` branch (user is null, i.e. initial login) to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` which requires `user != null`. This means passkeys conditional UI will no longer be rendered on the initial login page when no user has been identified yet. The tests in this PR (e.g. `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` and `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`) expect the webauthn form element to be present on the initial login page, which contradicts this code. The condition for the `authenticate` method should likely be `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` (without the user-null check) to preserve initial-login behavior while also enabling the re-authentication case.

findings.title: Passkeys no longer available on error during initial login
findings.body: The overridden `challenge(context, error, field)` method now only fills the webauthn context when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, which requires user != null. Previously it was `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`. This means that if a user enters an invalid username during initial login (user is still null after the failed attempt), the passkey option will not be shown on the error page, preventing them from retrying with a passkey. This is a UX regression for the initial-login error flow.

findings.title: Missing @Override annotation on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators
findings.body: The method `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(AuthenticationFlowContext context)` overrides `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` but is missing the `@Override` annotation. While not a runtime issue, this reduces compile-time safety and clarity of intent.
